text:
alex: Heads up — seeing a 2-3x p95 latency spike on kv-heavy long-context runs after last runtime rollout. Only reproduces under sustained batching load on a few FIFO machines. :eyes:

maria: Any quick traces? Was it during paging or pure eviction churn?

sam: Pulled a perf sample from one affected box. Top of flame: evicter_lock ~45%, request_handler ~30%, kv_reinsert ~15%. Looks like global evicter handshake is blocking hot path while it relocates tiny pages.

sam: Profiler snippet:
```
0.45 evicter_lock
0.30 request_handler
0.15 kv_reinsert
0.05 pager_io
0.05 other
```

jen: Could batching heuristics be amplifying the pressure? If kernel selection falls back to slower kernels under certain sequence lengths, each request holds KV residency longer -> higher concurrent live set.

alex: Good call. We saw a correlation: nodes with larger batch_max_tokens had higher eviction rate. When batch sizes balloon, more contexts concurrently reference KV and trigger reinsert work.

kai: I ran a quick repro script: `scripts/repro.sh --long-context 8192 --rate 200` — after ~12m the heap shows fragmentation: many 128B tombstones and ~30% allocator waste. FIFO reinserts leave tombstone chains.

maria: We also tried switching to LRU on two canaries. Latency improved, but we hit a correctness anomaly: in 1/100k traces there was stale KV reuse — trace t-9f3. Looks like reinserts and lookups race so LRU's reinsertion ordering exposed a window where an old KV pointer got reused.

sam: I added sequence numbers to KV entries in a debug build and reproduced a reinsert-vs-evict race: evicter unlinks an entry while request path re-inserts a new one with same slot id before the pager completes zeroing -> lookup may hit stale data.

sam: Minimal repro idea: two threads A (evict) and B (reinsert). Interleaving: A marks tombstone -> B allocates slot -> B writes meta but not seq -> A zeroes payload -> B writes payload -> B publishes -> readers may observe mismatch. Need atomic reinsert+publish or evict handshake.

jen: Operational mitigations: 1) temporarily lower batch_max_tokens and concurrency on FIFO fleets, 2) enable kv-prefetch-debounce to reduce thrash, 3) backport atomic publish for reinserts. Which is lowest risk?

alex: Quick canary plan: lower batch cap + kv-prefetch-debounce on 10% of traffic, monitor p95 and eviction rate. If that helps we can proceed with code fix for atomic publish.

kai: I'll try a prototype per-slab evict lock instead of one global lock — should reduce contention but may increase fragmentation. I can run a perf job with per-slab + batch cap 8.

maria: Note on correctness: if we move to per-slab locks we must ensure eviction/reinsert handshake still prevents the stale-publish window — sequence numbers alone aren't enough unless publish is a single atomic pointer swap.

sam: Agreed. Proposed code fix: make publish an atomic compare-and-swap of slot pointer after payload and seq are fully written. That plus a brief evict barrier should close the race without full global locking.

alex: Sounds like an action plan: (1) kai runs per-slab + batch cap experiment, (2) deploy canary with lower batch cap and kv-prefetch-debounce, (3) sam implements atomic publish fix in debug branch for verification. I'll file the rollout ticket and canary. :thumbsup:

deploy-bot: deploy scheduled to canary cluster (run id: 20240315-09).

jen: Thanks — please paste perf links and the flamegraph when available. :shipit:
